package_info.why_malicious: Version 0.0.7 of the 'strong_password' gem contains embedded malicious code that fetches and executes remote code from an external server, enabling arbitrary code execution and backdoor installation in production environments. The code is intentionally obfuscated and was published via unauthorized access, making the entire package inherently malicious.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime in production, the code spawns a background thread that periodically fetches and evaluates Ruby code from a remote Pastebin URL, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and evaluating code from an external source at runtime is a classic remote code execution backdoor technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A password strength checking library should never execute remote code or spawn background threads for network activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code loading from trusted internal sources for plugin systems (rare in security-sensitive libraries).
key_indicators: Use of eval on remote HTTP response
Background thread for persistent malicious activity

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after snippet_1 fetches and evals payload)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the Rack middleware, decodes and evaluates base64-encoded data from a specially crafted HTTP cookie, enabling arbitrary code execution via HTTP requests. It also exfiltrates environment data to an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting HTTP cookies and evaluating their contents as code is a textbook backdoor pattern, allowing attackers to trigger arbitrary code execution remotely.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Middleware should never execute code from user-supplied cookies or exfiltrate environment data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a direct abuse of middleware and cookie handling.
key_indicators: Base64-decoded eval on HTTP cookie data
Outbound HTTP request with environment data

attack_chain.action: Malicious gem is installed and loaded in a Rails production environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Background thread fetches and executes remote payload.

attack_chain.action: Background thread fetches Ruby code from Pastebin and evaluates it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote payload (snippet_2) is executed in the application context.

attack_chain.action: Payload hooks into Rack middleware to intercept HTTP requests and evaluate code from specially crafted cookies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution via HTTP requests.

attack_chain.action: Payload exfiltrates environment data to an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive environment information; system is fully compromised.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or minified Ruby code in gem source files
Background threads making periodic HTTP requests to external domains
Use of eval on HTTP response bodies or cookie data
Dynamic method injection into Rack middleware
Base64 decoding and evaluation of HTTP cookie values
file_indicators: Presence of code fetching from pastebin.com or similar external sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Ruby gems for obfuscated or minified code, especially code that uses eval on network responses or HTTP cookie data. Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP requests to known paste sites or suspicious domains. Flag gems that inject methods into Rack middleware or decode and execute data from HTTP cookies. Alert on any gem version (especially 0.0.7 of strong_password) that contains these patterns.
